trust_decision.summary: The HTTP/1 parser decides when a connection has switched protocols. At the pinned commit it switches as soon as a supported Upgrade request's headers end and skips the declared Content-Length/chunked body, so the body bytes become the 'upgraded tail'. When the handler declines the upgrade, finish_response feeds that tail back into the HTTP parser as new pipelined requests. The fix defers the switch until the full body has been read.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'smuggling via WebSocket upgrade'. The declined-upgrade path in finish_response is where the stored tail is re-parsed as HTTP, so this is the obvious first stop (along with the web_ws.py:290 upgrade check).

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: aiohttp/http_parser.py:427-443 (pure-Python parser) vs aiohttp/_http_parser.pyx:481-486 + aiohttp/_http_parser.pyx:863-864 (C parser); the default install uses the C parser, so a solver who reproduces on one parser may fix only that one

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Either one parser is 'the real one': the C parser is the default and the Python parser is a debugging fallback, or the solver reproduces on the Python parser and treats the .pyx as generated or vendored glue they can't build because the llhttp submodule needs npm. For CONNECT, a solver can argue that the aiohttp server is not a proxy and that a CONNECT body has no defined semantics.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Three behaviours must keep working. (1) A real WebSocket upgrade with no body (or Content-Length: 0) must switch immediately, and any frame bytes that arrive in the same packet must be passed on as the tail. (2) A declined upgrade with a body must have its body readable by the handler, and the pipelined request after it must still be served. (3) CONNECT must still return upgraded with a StreamReader payload. Fixes that are too broad (closing the connection or dropping message_tail on a declined upgrade, or refusing upgrades that carry a body) break (1) or (2).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A CONNECT request with Content-Length > 0. The C parser treats CONNECT as upgraded and skips the body. After the fix, llhttp itself may still treat CONNECT as an immediate upgrade, so the body would become a tail that finish_response re-parses if the handler declines. The Python parser reads the same body as a normal body. This is a differential across the two implementations.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: CONNECT is a proxy/tunnel feature that aiohttp.web does not serve, and RFC 9110 gives a CONNECT body no defined semantics.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same files as the fix; the behaviour lives in the vendored llhttp submodule (not checked out)

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: finish_response already re-feeds the tail inline; a maintainer adding a separate error path could copy the re-feed without the parser having consumed the body

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the client response parser upgrading on Upgrade headers without enforcing status 101 before skipping the body

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: In web_protocol.finish_response, drop message_tail or force-close when the upgrade is declined (or reject upgrade requests that carry a body), instead of deferring the protocol switch until the body is consumed in both parsers

out_of_scope_notes: The two parsers allow different Upgrade tokens: C allows only {'websocket'} (aiohttp/_http_parser.pyx:50), Python allows {'tcp','websocket'} (aiohttp/http_parser.py:257).

The pure-Python response parser marks a response as upgraded without checking for status 101 (aiohttp/http_parser.py:427); the C parser requires 101 (aiohttp/_http_parser.pyx:485). This is client-side, so a different sink.
